chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about fasting the Day of 'Arafah. He said: 'Whoever is strong enough for it, it is good, provided it does not prevent you from supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking [of God]. So fast it, but if you fear that you will become weak in doing so, then do not fast it.' As for fasting the Day of 'Ashura, encouragement for fasting it has come, and dislike [for it] has also come. As for what was narrated regarding encouragement for fasting it, it has been narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the Day of 'Arafah and Day of 'Ashura in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a pragmatic hierarchy for fasting the Day of 'Arafah, prioritizing the spiritual potency of supplication over the physical act of fasting, thereby reflecting the Shia emphasis on *du'a* as a primary mode of worship. Regarding 'Ashura, he acknowledges the scholarly divergence between narrations encouraging fasting to expiate sins and those discouraging it to distinguish from the Sunnah of the pre-Islamic era, illustrating the methodological nuance in reconciling conflicting reports within the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
